classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange each equation before solving, including converting cosecant to sine and recognising a sine-to-cosine quotient as tangent while checking zero cosine. Then select quadrants and round to minutes.

content.prompt: Solve the following for $\theta\in[0^\circ,360^\circ]$, giving answers to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}5\cos\theta&=2\\\cos\theta&=\frac25\end{align*}$$
Let $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(\frac25)$. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha,\ 360^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx66^\circ25',293^\circ35'\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}\theta&=-\frac43\\\sin\theta&=-\frac34\end{align*}$$
Let $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(\frac34)$. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ+\alpha,\ 360^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx228^\circ35',311^\circ25'\end{align*}$$

If $\cos\theta=0$, the original equation is not satisfied. Divide by $\cos\theta$:
$$\begin{align*}2\tan\theta&=5\\\tan\theta&=\frac52\end{align*}$$
Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(\frac52)$. Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha,\ 180^\circ+\alpha\\\theta&\approx68^\circ12',248^\circ12'\end{align*}$$
